hints: Focus on what alkaline aqueous iodine is really testing for, the iodoform test for a specific small group in the molecule.
Look for the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group or the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, and check which of the four structures contains one of these.
Now test the survivors for chirality by looking for a carbon with four different groups, and keep the one with no chiral centre.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform test**

A positive test with alkaline aqueous iodine means a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$. This happens only if the molecule has a methyl carbonyl group or a group that can form one.

Positive group: $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$

**Check each compound for the iodoform group**

Compound A, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, has $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so positive. Compound C, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(OH)CH}_3$, also has $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so positive.

Compound B, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CHO}$, has $\text{CH(OH)}$ but it is not $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so negative. Compound D, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C(OH)CHO}$, has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so negative.

**Check the survivors for optical isomerism**

Optical isomerism needs a chiral centre, a carbon with four different groups attached. Look carefully at A and C.

In A: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C(=O)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}$, both $\text{CH}_2$ groups have two H atoms, so no chiral centre. In C: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C(=O)}-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_3$, the $\text{CH(OH)}$ carbon is bonded to H, OH, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{COCH}_3$, so it is chiral.

**Combine both conditions**

We need positive iodoform AND no chirality. Only compound A satisfies both, so it is the answer.

options.A: Contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ so gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate with $\text{I}_2$ in $\text{NaOH}$. It has no carbon with four different groups, the chain is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, so it is achiral and shows no optical isomerism.
options.B: Fails the iodoform test because it has neither $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ nor $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$. It also fails the second condition because the $\text{CH(OH)}$ carbon is attached to $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-$, H, OH and CHO, so it is chiral and would show optical isomerism.
options.C: Gives a positive iodoform test due to $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, which is a common trap. However the $\text{CH(OH)}$ carbon is bonded to four different groups (H, OH, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{COCH}_3$), so it is chiral and does show optical isomerism, so it must be rejected.
options.D: Has no chiral centre because the central C has two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups, which is tempting. However it gives a negative iodoform test because it has neither $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ nor $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, it is a tertiary alcohol next to an aldehyde.
